text:
sasha: hey team, customer 'acme-app' reports repeated partial SSE events and reconnect storms when going through their gRPC-web gateway (they're using grpcwebproxy + nginx). happens only when traffic flows via our HTTP/2 frontend -> gRPC gateway -> backend conversion path. raw symptom: client receives first 1-2 lines of an event then connection drops, client reconnects (with Last-Event-ID) and sometimes sees duplicate tokens billed. they opened a support ticket: https://acme.example/ticket/4421 :grimace:

miguel: can you paste the original request/response examples? headers and any proxy logs would help.

sasha: pasted minimal repro below. note: customer is using browser fetch with EventSource polyfill (gRPC-web uses text/event-stream after translate). reproduction (server is our streaming API endpoint):

```bash
# baseline that works direct to our hosted api (http2)
curl -v --http2-prior-knowledge -N \"https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/stream?model=gpt-foo\"
```

server sent chunks like:

```
event: message
data: {"chunk":"Hello"}

event: message
data: {"chunk":" world"}

:keepalive

```

but through the customer's path they see truncated payloads, e.g. only `event: message\ndata: {"chunk":"Hello"}` then a TCP/TLS close. curl against the gateway shows a reset on stream: `HTTP/2 stream 1 RST_STREAM 0x1 (REFUSED_STREAM)` then connection persists. nginx/proxy logs attached: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream` and `recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)`.

anna: interesting. gRPC-web -> SSE conversions often glue framing. Two things to watch: 1) trailing headers (we use trailers for billing/usage tokens); many proxies drop or buffer trailers. 2) chunk flush semantics - if the gateway buffers until newline or until buffer full, browser's EventSource gets partial events and times out.

jamie: our infra-side envoy/gRPC-web config historically sets `grpc_http2_max_stream_duration` and also has a filter that re-encodes frames. If a proxy emits `RST_STREAM` with REFUSED_STREAM, that usually means upstream reset the stream (maybe backend closed because it thought client gone). might be keepalive mismatch between ALB and gateway.

sasha: repro steps the customer used (they included):
1) Start grpcwebproxy that converts gRPC -> http1 for browser.
2) NGINX in front to terminate TLS and proxy_pass to grpcwebproxy. NGINX has `proxy_buffering on` by default.
3) Browser connects via EventSource polyfill.

They tried disabling `proxy_buffering off` and that reduced truncation frequency but duplicates/billing still happened.

miguel: can you share server-side logs around the RST_STREAM? we should check if our runtime emitted a FIN/close after writing partial chunk (maybe due to a bug where we drop KV cache for streaming sessions on certain errors).

sasha: here's an excerpt from our runtime logs (redacted):

```
[2023-08-19T16:12:02Z] connection 10.2.1.8:443 stream=1 WRITE 512 bytes
[2023-08-19T16:12:02Z] connection 10.2.1.8:443 stream=1 FLUSH
[2023-08-19T16:12:02Z] connection 10.2.1.8:443 stream=1 ERROR: upstream write failed: broken pipe
[2023-08-19T16:12:02Z] connection 10.2.1.8:443 stream=1 CLOSE reason=client_close
```

anna: broken pipe on write indicates the other side closed. That aligns with NGINX earlier. Could be the gRPC-web proxy translating larger streaming frames into multiple HTTP/1.1 chunks and NGINX buffering dropping due to timeouts. Also many gateways don't forward HTTP/2 trailers (which we use to attach final usage metadata). If a client reconnects and doesn't get the final 'id' trailer we emit, they may replay and cause duplicate billing.

sasha: customer attached tcpdump showing FIN gaps and TCP retransmits after ~120s mark. They also have AWS ALB in front of NGINX with idle timeout 60s.

jamie: ah that could be the root: ALB idle timeout < long-lived SSE. ALB closes the connection, proxy/proxy_chain sends RST/FIN back to upstream which triggers our runtime to mark session closed and emit final usage metrics — but because client reconnects without consistent event:id we re-bill.

miguel: suggested mitigations:
- add SSE `id:` fields (we can emit event ids or use Last-Event-ID support) so client reconnection is idempotent.
- ensure proxies preserve trailers or include a per-stream-id header earlier so billing can dedupe server-side.
- set X-Accel-Buffering: no (nginx) and proxy_buffering off
- ensure ALB/ELB idle timeout >= streaming session SLO (or use TCP keepalive ping)

anna: also check grpcwebproxy settings: there is an option `-run_http_server` vs `-run_grpc_server` that changes how streaming frames are flushed. recommend testing with `grpcwebproxy --backend_addr=127.0.0.1:8080 --allow_all_origins --run_http_server` and curl --no-buffer to simulate.

lia-cs: customer is worried about charges; they've requested we pause billing while we repro. can billing freeze while we investigate?

jamie: escalate to finance? but we can add server-side safeguards to avoid double-counting in short-term: use server dedupe window keyed by `x-client-session-id` (customer can set) so repeated reconnect within 2m doesn't double-bill. I'll create a dev task.

sasha: quick debugging tips i used:
- curl through path: `curl -v -N --http1.1 https://nginx-front.example/stream` (some gateways only speak http1 to backend)
- simulate small writes + flush from our runtime to see how gateway buffers: `printf 'event: message\ndata: hi\n\n' | nc -l 8080` then proxy through nginx
- inspect `nginx -V` for `--with-http_stub_status_module` and check `proxy_buffering` settings

miguel: i dug into runtime code; there is a code path where if upstream write gets EPIPE we call closeSession() which currently writes final billing trailer via http2 trailers. if the proxy has already torn down the stream, trailers are never observed. plan: change to persist session record to storage before writing trailers and only emit bill event on successful trailer ack. fallback: emit a short JSON heartbeat with partial billing info inline in a chunked event so proxies will pass it.

anna: for immediate customer-facing workaround: add `Retry-After: 0` ? no that doesn't help. better: send an SSE `event: session` with `data: {"session_id":"<id>","partial":true}` periodically. that gives client a stable id to pass back on reconnect. also tell them to set ALB idle timeout to 350s while we test.

sasha: i responded to customer with triage steps and asked them to test `proxy_buffering off` and ALB timeout increase. they did that and reported big improvement but occasional duplications still occurred.

jamie: created infra ticket INFRA-1127 to add explicit idle-timeout docs for streaming customers and a config guide for nginx/grpcwebproxy/envoy.

miguel: created runtime PR #2486 that: 1) persists stream metadata before final trailers, 2) adds an inline final-chunk with minimal billing info if trailers fail to be delivered, and 3) emits an `event: id` every 15s.

sasha: pushed update to customer to try canary endpoint (no trailers, inline final-chunk). they tested for 24h and no duplicate charges seen. customer asked for an engineering postmortem.

anna: notes for postmortem: root cause = mismatch of streaming semantics across HTTP/2 frontend -> HTTP/1.1 gRPC-web translation -> nginx buffering -> ALB idle timeouts, combined with runtime assumption that trailers are reliable. contributing factor = missing stream id in SSE payload for idempotency.

lia-cs: customer pleased, asked for config snippets we used. can we paste the nginx + grpcwebproxy example?

sasha: sample nginx snippet i gave them:

```nginx
server {
  listen 443 ssl;
  location / {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    proxy_set_header Connection \"keep-alive\";
    proxy_buffering off; # critical for flush semantics
    proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no;
    proxy_read_timeout 360s;
  }
}
```

and grpcwebproxy run args:

```
grpcwebproxy --backend_addr=127.0.0.1:8081 --allow_all_origins --run_http_server --backend_tls=false
```

miguel: action items:
- runtime: land PR #2486 and deploy canary (assigned miguel)
- infra: publish streaming proxy configuration guide and update ALB idle timeout recommendations (assigned jamie)
- cs: confirm billing freeze/adjustment for acme-app if dup charges found (lia-cs)
- docs: add SSE idempotency recommendations to API docs (anna)

sasha: customer has accepted canary and will run with it for a week. marking thread as monitoring. thanks all :raised_hands:

infra-bot: INFRA-1127 created and assigned to jamie (priority: P2)

miguel: follow-up: i also added metrics to detect RST_STREAM with REFUSED_STREAM origin so we can alert early if proxies become aggressive.

lia-cs: customer wants a short writeup for execs — i'll draft based on this thread and ping for approvals.

sasha: closing loop for now, will reopen if duplicates reappear.
